newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bonds have a little upside leg room.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds have a little upside leg room.

text.p: September Treasury bond futures are likely to stretch the current rally to another new peak before a pullback is in order, technicians and traders said Friday.
"The floor definitely feels there is more room on the upside," said a broker on the Chicago Board of Trade floor.
However, many participants are looking up with an eye to sell, he said. He identified 115-21 and 115-28 as levels where he would be inclined to get short.
Futures were last trading at 115-06/32, down 4/32, after recovering from a dip on strong June durable goods orders.

Joe Plauche, financial futures analyst for Dean Witter, said he was looking for September futures to extend the latest leg of the uptrend to 115-28/32 or 116-00 by Monday or Tuesday based on Elliott Wave analysis.

The area represents a fifth-wave target, he said. Noting the contract has been trending up since April ll, Plauche said Wednesday's 115-23/32 high in September bonds concluded wave three of a five-wave upmove off the July 15 low of 113-07/32.
Today's session low so far of 114-28/32 constitutes wave four, he said. At 115-23/32, September bond futures were at their highest point in a year and a half.
To complete wave five, the contract needs to exceed 115-23/32. From there, Plauche predicted a pullback to about 114-24/32. "We're approaching a top of some importance," he said.

Underscoring that sentiment are stochastics and momentum studies that failed to reach a new peak along with futures Wednesday. "Those sorts of divergences are symptomatic of the formation of a top," said Plauche.
Holly Liss, assistant vice president of technical analysis for Sakura Dellsher, said candlestick charts and probability statistics were also pointing to a retrenchment.
A "doji star" on daily candlestick charts Thursday came close to confirming the bearish "shooting star" established Wednesday, she said.
"If we continue with this corrective type of pattern, it looks like we could get down to the 114-12/32 to 114-09/32 area short term," Liss said.
Probability theory that takes into account price volatility now also suggests a pullback, said the analyst.
"Odds favor the market's going to move lower by a point rather than higher by a point from current levels, Liss said.
She set a timeframe within the August 23 expiration of September bond options for the downturn, but cautioned that a close above 115-14/32 would negate the downside objective.
